record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Effect of phase transitions on QSO dynamics
record.original_question: When a quadratic stochastic operator is generated by a Gibbs measure associated with a Hamiltonian H on a continuous state space, and the Gibbs measure may be non-unique because the corresponding physical system has a phase transition, how does the thermodynamic phase transition affect the behavior of the trajectories of the associated QSO?

evidence.quote: More precisely, if E is continual set then one can associate the Gibbs measure µ by a Hamiltonian H (defined on E) and temperature T > 0 [37]. It is known that depending on the Hamiltonian and the values of the temperature the measure µ can be non unique. In this case there is a phase transition of the physical system with the Hamiltonian H.
Problem 16. (by N.N.Ganikhodjaev) How the thermodynamics (the phase transition) will effect to behavior of the trajectories of a QSO corresponding to a Gibbs measure of the Hamiltonian H?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(E,\mathcal{B})$ be a measurable space (the state space, taken to be a continuum). Let $S(E,\mathcal{B})$ denote the set of all probability measures on $(E,\mathcal{B})$. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) is a map $V: S(E,\mathcal{B})\to S(E,\mathcal{B})$ defined by
$$(V\lambda)(A) \;=\; \int_E\!\!\int_E P(x,y,A)\,d\lambda(x)\,d\lambda(y), \qquad A\in\mathcal{B},$$
where $P(\cdot,\cdot,\cdot)$ is a measurable family of probability kernels satisfying $P(x,y,\cdot)=P(y,x,\cdot)$ for all $x,y\in E$. The trajectory of an initial measure $\lambda^{(0)}\in S(E,\mathcal{B})$ is the sequence $\lambda^{(n)} = V^n\lambda^{(0)}$, $n\ge 0$.

Suppose now that the kernel $P$ is constructed from a Gibbs measure $\mu$ on $E$ associated with a Hamiltonian $H:E\to\mathbb{R}$ at temperature $T>0$, so that the QSO $V=V_{H,T}$ is generated by this Gibbs measure. For Hamiltonians $H$ and temperatures $T$ at which the system exhibits a phase transition (i.e. the Gibbs measure associated with $(H,T)$ is non-unique), describe how this non-uniqueness/phase transition manifests itself in the dynamical behavior of the trajectories $\{V_{H,T}^n\lambda^{(0)}\}_{n\ge 0}$. In particular, determine the relationship between the set of limit points (or fixed points, periodic orbits, ergodic averages) of the QSO dynamics and the simplex of Gibbs measures for $(H,T)$, and show how crossing a phase-transition threshold changes the asymptotic behavior of trajectories.
artifact.category_tag: Quadratic stochastic operators and Gibbs measures
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal active research on QSOs generated by Gibbs distributions (e.g., works of Ganikhodjaev, Rozikov, Jamilov) and on phase-transition phenomena in lattice models, but no source providing a general answer linking thermodynamic phase transitions to the trajectory behavior of QSOs on continuous state spaces was found. The problem appears to remain open in this generality.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators and Their Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of QSO dynamics including those generated by Gibbs measures, listing open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The interaction between Gibbs-measure non-uniqueness and QSO trajectory behavior is discussed as an open direction.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Ergodic Properties and Their Applications
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) survey treating ergodic properties of QSOs and listing remaining open questions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys still treat the phase-transition/QSO-trajectory question as not fully resolved.
